en.html:
Valid point.

We had come on and on along what was not a road. More precisely, it seemed a road had once held a position here and then resigned. We were following its former intentions. Here it probably went straight. There it apparently had an argument with some roots.

For a pleasant hike, you would have to be a very special fellow to select this route. Somebody who enjoyed walking but felt the feet were enjoying it too much.

en.html: Left alone so long, who knew when the roof would come down? Probably why entry was banned—◆no, yaar. That too, but not the main problem. If Suzukawa was right, this might be the culprit's operating base. Surely the fellow was not living here... but even that possibility we could not throw away. Walking in casually did not look like the clever option. The roof might kill us by accident; somebody inside might have actual enthusiasm for the work. Neither needed us to make it easier. I tried to stop him. No effect. He kept going toward the building. The three of us looked at each other. Same hesitation, same confusion. Nobody had brought a different expression. We might as well have looked in a mirror and asked that fellow for leadership. Finally Tadayasu shrugged and followed him. One step later, Konatsu and I went too. ...This far we had come. Ab toh we had to commit.
en.text:
Left alone so long, who knew when the roof would come down? Probably why entry was banned—◆no, yaar. That too, but not the main problem.

If Suzukawa was right, this might be the culprit's operating base. Surely the fellow was not living here... but even that possibility we could not throw away.

Walking in casually did not look like the clever option. The roof might kill us by accident; somebody inside might have actual enthusiasm for the work. Neither needed us to make it easier.

I tried to stop him. No effect. He kept going toward the building.

The three of us looked at each other. Same hesitation, same confusion. Nobody had brought a different expression. We might as well have looked in a mirror and asked that fellow for leadership.

Finally Tadayasu shrugged and followed him. One step later, Konatsu and I went too.

...This far we had come. Ab toh we had to commit.

en.html:
Dust. Mould. Dry, rotting wood.

Haan, those smells I had prepared for. An abandoned building would smell like an abandoned building.

But this sour stink crushing all three beneath it—what was THIS?

Something like it, I knew. A very ordinary smell. At home, at school, on the road also.

Slowly, my eyes began to manage the dim light.

en.html:
Looked like a classroom.

No desks or chairs. Perhaps they had taken those when they abandoned the place. Put them back and even now it might just about pass for somewhere to study. Education could survive a surprising amount of unhappiness in its surroundings. Students already knew that.

Suzukawa was not visible.

Instead, four large boxes stood where the teacher's platform should be. Substitute teachers, surely not. Though all four were keeping their thoughts to themselves, which was a promising improvement.

The smell seemed to be coming from there.

All sorts of things mixed together. Garbage-dump type.

en.html:
Thank you, professor. That much we also knew.

Why were we all standing here doing discussion? Because nobody wanted to open the bloody thing. We were hoping to understand the contents through the combined power of saying what they might be. Very advanced method. If successful, hands would become unnecessary.

Bad smell but good contents: fermented kusaya fish, cheese, durian. Very short list. Everything else smelled terrible because it was terrible. My nose was not a pessimist; it was giving sensible advice.

But Suzukawa was missing. Roaming blindly through the place, I did not want to do either. Apart from checking the smell, what useful action was available? Standing and waiting was making me restless.

...Chalo. Fine.

en.html:
I went toward the boxes, very carefully, hoping a whole rat population would not come flying out.

Plastic. No lock. Just a lid resting on top, apparently.

Easy opening. Wah. A lock would have been so helpful. Sorry, friends, impossible, let us respect the lock. But the bloody box was cooperating fully.

I poked the side a couple of times.

A faint slosh.

Tadayasu's nose had supplied correct information.

Hand on the edge. One deep breath. Hold it.

I lifted the lid.

en.html:
Almost.

I almost fell down right there.

Kya—!?
WHAT WAS THAT SMELL?

Bad smell? No.
Not bad smell.
Not that small a thing.

Violence.
The smell was beating me.

So foul my brain recognised it a moment late. Like putting your hand on a boiling kettle before knowing it was hot.

This smell I did not know.
Nahin, I knew it...

WHICH ONE!?

Not this smell. But a smell that could become this—that I knew.

It was.
It was.

Was it shaking my brain also?

The room tilted. I stumbled.

One hand grabbed the box's edge for support. Wrong place, apparently. The box turned over at once and threw everything onto the floor.

en.html:
Konatsu was shouting something.

Arre, so much noise. How will I think? Dekh, now I had forgotten what I was thinking!

What was it. Kya tha.

Haan, uniform. Uniform and bag.
What else was there. What else could I see.

Something between the folds of the uniform.
What was that.

Who was waving a hand in front of my eyes? Hata, yaar. You're blocking it.

Tadayasu? No, he was sitting on the floor. Why sit there? Trousers would get dirty.

Arre, I couldn't see.
WHOSE HAND?

Achha. Mine.

Move, then. I wanted to see what was there.

And neck, you also! Don't turn away by yourself!
Look properly, na.

What was there.
What was there.

Uniform.
Inside it.

　ちゃんと見ろよ。

　何がある。

　制服。
　その中身。
